transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Do not touch the washing machine, plug, socket, or any water around them. Do not try to pull the plug out while the floor is wet.

1. Keep everyone away from the kitchen, especially children/pets. Avoid stepping in the water.
2. If you can reach your consumer unit/fuse box without crossing the wet area, switch off the washing-machine circuit or, if unsure, switch off the main electricity supply.
• If you cannot do this safely, leave it alone and do not enter the water.
3. Once power is definitely off, turn off the washing machine’s water supply valve if it is accessible without standing in water. It is usually on the hose behind/near the machine; turn clockwise.
4. Do not restart the machine or use that socket until it has been checked and the area is completely dry.
5. If water is near the socket/plug, has gone under units, or you suspect an electrical hazard, contact an electrician urgently. In the UK, for an immediate electrical danger or damaged supply equipment call 105; call 999 if there is smoke, sparks, fire, or someone has had an electric shock.

After the power is isolated, you can use towels to contain water only if it is safe to do so. Arrange a washing-machine engineer/plumber to find the leak before using it again.
oh god I'm standing in the wet in my socks right now, should I just step out? The fuse box is in the hall so I can get to that without the water, I'll go and switch it off now

Yes — step out of the wet area immediately, carefully, without touching the washing machine, socket, plug, metal sink/taps, or any appliances.

Once you are on a dry floor:

1. Go to the fuse box in the hall.
2. Switch off the main power switch if you are not completely sure which circuit supplies the kitchen/washing machine. Do not go back into the kitchen until it is off.
3. Keep others out of the kitchen.
4. After power is off, turn off the washing machine’s water valve if you can reach it without standing in water.

If you felt any tingle/shock, have burns, chest pain, weakness, or feel unwell, call 999 now. If there are sparks, smoke, buzzing, or a burning smell, do not re-enter — call 999.

ok I've stepped out onto the dry hall floor and switched the main power off at the fuse box. I didn't feel any tingle or shock. The water tap for the machine is behind it so I can't reach it without standing in the water. What now?

Good — stay on the dry hall floor and leave the main power off.

Do not go back into the water to reach behind the machine or move it.

Next:

1. Take off your wet socks and dry your feet, so you do not slip or track water elsewhere.
2. If you know where your home’s main water stopcock is and can reach it from a dry area — commonly under the kitchen sink, near the water meter, or in a utility cupboard — turn it clockwise to stop the water supply to the whole property.
• Only do this if you can access it without entering the flooded area.
3. If you cannot reach a stopcock safely, call an emergency plumber, your landlord/building manager if applicable, or a washing-machine repair service. Tell them: “The washing machine is leaking, water is under the units and near the electrical socket; the main electricity is switched off.”
4. Keep the electricity off. Do not switch it back on just because the machine stops or the visible floor dries.
5. Once the water supply is stopped and there is no electrical risk, use towels from the dry edge to limit the spread if you can do so without stepping into the water. Water that has reached sockets/under units needs time to dry and may need an electrician to inspect before power is restored.

If you see smoke, sparks, hear crackling/buzzing, or smell burning, stay out of the kitchen and call 999.
